messages:
linda-support: FYI customer ACME hit a sudden spike of 429s right after today's rate policy push (canary rollout rlp-2026-03-17). They report ~30% of requests got 429 in a 5m window. sample header they sent: `x-request-id: acme-req-8f3a` and `x-rate-limit-policy: v2`
rahul-eng-platform: thanks — are these in the canary cohort (10%) or from the old policy path? can you paste a short request/response pair (strip PII) and timestamp? :eyes:
linda-support: looks like canary. pasted snippet below (sanitized):
```
> GET /v1/generate
> Host: api.redwood.ai
> x-api-key: <redacted>
> x-request-id: acme-req-8f3a

< HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
< Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2026 12:17:42 GMT
< Retry-After: 5
< X-RateLimit-Limit: 120
< X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
< X-RateLimit-Reset: 1616080662
```

amelia-eng-sre: quick check — monitoring shows short-lived 429 spike in us-west-2 at 12:16-12:22 UTC aligning with canary traffic shift. error rate went from ~0.5% to 6% for that customer. traces show `throttled=true` at gateway.
ops-bot: ALERT: rollout/rlp-2026-03-17 canary error_rate > 5% in us-west-2 (10m window) — auto-notify to #eng-sre & #support.
mike-oncall: please pause the canary traffic. rahul, can you stop the rollout or flip traffic back to v1 for the canary cohort?
rahul-eng-platform: doing it now — calling admin API: `POST /admin/rollouts/rlp-2026-03-17/actions` body `{ "action": "pause" }` 
rahul-eng-platform: response `200 OK` — canary paused, scaling of v2 instances reduced, traffic routing reverted for cohort id `canary-10pct` :white_check_mark:
linda-support: confirming ACME reports error rate dropped to baseline within 90s. they're unblocked for now. they asked what went wrong so we can follow up.
amelia-eng-sre: early hypothesis: the new rate policy has a stricter burst window combined with gateway batching change — for a subset of clients with bursty patterns we under-provisioned token buckets. need to compare `burst_limit` and `refill_rate` metrics between v1 and v2.
rahul-eng-platform: agreed. I'll fetch rollout diff and runtime config: `GET /admin/rollouts/rlp-2026-03-17/diff` and send config snapshot.
rahul-eng-platform: diff shows `burst_limit` decreased from `50` -> `20` for path `/v1/generate` and `bucket_refill` unchanged. that explains client-visible 429s on short bursts.
amelia-eng-sre: next steps: 1) create a quick patch to restore burst_limit to 50 in v2 and redeploy to canary OR 2) keep rollout paused and do a config hotfix. prefer hotfix. I'll open emergency config PR and run a small canary (2%) after tests.
mike-oncall: +1 for hotfix and small canary. also let's run a retrospective and update the rollout checklist to include synthetic burst tests.
linda-support: I'll reply to ACME with timeline: paused canary, errors resolved, we'll follow up with root cause and timeline for fix. asked them to send any additional `x-request-id`s if they see further 429s. :pray:
rahul-eng-platform: created config PR: `cfg/rollouts/rlp-2026-03-17/restore-burst` — CI passing. will apply to canary once SRE gives thumbs.
amelia-eng-sre: applying hotfix to canary now (`/admin/configs/apply?target=canary-10pct&cfg=restore-burst`) — patch applied. running 5 minute smoke.
amelia-eng-sre: smoke looks good. error rate at 0.6% now. proceeding to a 2% canary expansion for 20m.
linda-support: ACME confirms no more 429s. closing the immediate escalation. filing a post-incident note and adding synthetic burst tests to rollout QA checklist.
mike-oncall: nice work team. please add follow-up item to eng-platform backlog: ensure rollout diffs surface `burst_limit` changes prominently. :memo:
ops-bot: NOTE: Incident closed for rollout/rlp-2026-03-17 canary spike. Follow-up ticket #INF-4923 created.
